turns.text: My hiking partner just got bitten on the calf by a rattlesnake and we're two hours from the trailhead. What's the correct first aid, in order?
Why do they say to keep him still? What does moving do to the venom?
How should I position the leg, and should I take off his boot?
If I could reach a ranger, what would they tell me to do while we wait?
What do emergency doctors want to know when a snakebite arrives — what should I note down?
A friend said to mark the edge of the swelling with a pen and the time. Is that right, and why?
Someone else told me to remove rings and anything tight. Why does that matter?
There's no phone signal and he's panicking. How do I keep him calm and decide whether to carry him or wait?
What signs would mean he's getting worse fast, and what do I do then?
Can you give me a step-by-step plan — first aid, moving him, what to watch for, and how to get help the moment we have signal?
